extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news organizations, journalism students, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational 'About' page describing the Nieman Journalism Lab's mission, activities, staff, licensing and fellowship deadlines; intended to explain what the Lab does and how people can engage with or reuse its content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Journalism Lab is an attempt to help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab’s editorial focus is to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail; to find good ideas for others to steal; to help reporters and editors adjust to online work; to help traditional news organizations find ways to survive; and to help new startups that will complement or supplant them. The Lab positions itself as optimistic and collaborative in pursuing these aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader contributions and collaborative exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary among them are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas. Tell us what's happening around you, or what should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explicitly invites reader participation — sending tips, examples, or ideas — and frames the Lab as a community resource shaped in part by its audience. Engagement (subscribing, following, contributing) is part of how the Lab operates and curates coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership of site content
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is © the President and Fellows of Harvard College or the content’s original author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default ownership is with Harvard or the original author; users should attribute content to Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the author, preferably with a link back to the original content. For reuse beyond the site license, the page invites contact to request permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content reuse license: Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Also unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuse conditions specified: (a) not for commercial purposes, (b) attribute to Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the author (preferably with a link back), and (c) release derivative works under a similar license. The page gives concrete examples of permitted uses (translating the site into Portuguese, redistributing posts to students, using the Twitter feed in a song) and asks to be informed of interesting uses; it also invites contact for other types of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowship application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual deadline to apply for a fellowship is December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement for applicants to the Nieman Foundation fellowships; applicants should note the annual deadlines by applicant type (international vs. American).
